passages.text: “Hear this, O priests! Take heed, O house of Israel! Give ear, O royal house! For this judgment is against you because you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Hosea speaks to the leaders of Israel.
He addresses the priests.
He addresses the people of Israel.
He addresses the royal house.
He commands them to listen.
He says, “Hear this, O priests.”
He says, “Pay attention, house of Israel.”
He says, “Listen, royal house.”
He declares that judgment is coming against them.
He says, “This judgment is for you.”
He explains the reason for judgment.
He says, “You have been a snare at Mizpah.”
He says, “You have spread a net on Tabor.”
He accuses them of leading others into sin.
He holds them responsible for their actions.
passages.original: שִׁמְעוּ־ זֹ֨את הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים וְהַקְשִׁ֣יבוּ׀ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּבֵ֤ית הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַאֲזִ֔ינוּ כִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם הַמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּֽי־ פַח֙ הֱיִיתֶ֣ם לְמִצְפָּ֔ה וְרֶ֖שֶׁת פְּרוּשָׂ֥ה עַל־ תָּבֽוֹר׃

passages.text: The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I will chastise them all.
passages.sermon:
The rebels act violently.
They kill many people.
They go deeper into evil.
I am the Lord.
I will punish all of them.
passages.original: וְשַׁחֲטָ֥ה שֵׂטִ֖ים הֶעְמִ֑יקוּ וַאֲנִ֖י מוּסָ֥ר לְכֻלָּֽם׃

passages.text: I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me. For now, O Ephraim, you have turned to prostitution; Israel is defiled.
passages.sermon:
God knows Ephraim completely.
Israel is not hidden from God.
Ephraim has turned to prostitution.
Israel is now defiled.
passages.original: אֲנִי֙ יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹֽא־ נִכְחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ הִזְנֵ֣יתָ אֶפְרַ֔יִם נִטְמָ֖א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel have turned away from God.
Their actions stop them from coming back to Him.
A spirit of prostitution lives inside them.
They do not know the LORD.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יִתְּנוּ֙ מַ֣עַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם לָשׁ֖וּב אֶל־ אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ זְנוּנִים֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔ם וְאֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity; even Judah stumbles with them.
passages.sermon:
Israel is proud.
This pride stands as a witness against Israel.
Israel sins.
Ephraim sins.
Israel and Ephraim stumble because of their sins.
Judah also stumbles with them.
passages.original: וְעָנָ֥ה גְאֽוֹן־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָנָ֑יו וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וְאֶפְרַ֗יִם יִכָּֽשְׁלוּ֙ בַּעֲוֺנָ֔ם כָּשַׁ֥ל גַּם־ יְהוּדָ֖ה עִמָּֽם׃

passages.text: They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, but they do not find Him; He has withdrawn Himself from them.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel take their flocks and herds.
They go to seek the LORD.
They do not find the LORD.
The LORD has withdrawn Himself from them.
passages.original: בְּצֹאנָ֣ם וּבִבְקָרָ֗ם יֵֽלְכ֛וּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָ֑אוּ חָלַ֖ץ מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They have been unfaithful to the LORD; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the New Moon will devour them along with their land.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel have betrayed the LORD.
They have acted unfaithfully toward God.
They have given birth to children who do not belong to Him.
Now a new month will come.
This new month will destroy them.
It will also destroy their land.
passages.original: בַּיהוָ֣ה בָּגָ֔דוּ כִּֽי־ בָנִ֥ים זָרִ֖ים יָלָ֑דוּ עַתָּ֛ה יֹאכְלֵ֥ם חֹ֖דֶשׁ אֶת־ חֶלְקֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; raise the battle cry in Beth-aven: Lead on, O Benjamin!
passages.sermon:
The prophet Hosea speaks to the people of Israel.
He commands them to sound an alarm.
He says, “Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah.”
He says, “Blow the trumpet in Ramah.”
He says, “Raise the battle cry in Beth-aven.”
He calls Benjamin to lead the way.
passages.original: תִּקְע֤וּ שׁוֹפָר֙ בַּגִּבְעָ֔ה חֲצֹצְרָ֖ה בָּרָמָ֑ה הָרִ֙יעוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אָ֔וֶן אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ בִּנְיָמִֽין׃

passages.text: Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
God will punish Ephraim.
Ephraim will become a wasteland.
This will happen on the day God rebukes them.
God speaks to all the tribes of Israel.
God announces what is true and certain.
passages.original: אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה בְּי֖וֹם תּֽוֹכֵחָ֑ה בְּשִׁבְטֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הוֹדַ֖עְתִּי נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃

passages.text: The princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones; I will pour out My fury upon them like water.
passages.sermon:
The princes of Judah act like people who move boundary stones.
They change the borders dishonestly.
I will pour out My fury on them.
My anger will come like water.
passages.original: הָיוּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה כְּמַסִּיגֵ֖י גְּב֑וּל עֲלֵיהֶ֕ם אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹךְ כַּמַּ֖יִם עֶבְרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim is oppressed.
Ephraim is crushed in judgment.
Ephraim is determined to follow worthless idols.
passages.original: עָשׁ֥וּק אֶפְרַ֖יִם רְצ֣וּץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֣י הוֹאִ֔יל הָלַ֖ךְ אַחֲרֵי־ צָֽו׃

passages.text: So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God compares Himself to a moth for Ephraim.
God acts like a moth that slowly destroys cloth.
God compares Himself to decay for the house of Judah.
God acts like decay that slowly ruins wood or bones.
God brings slow destruction to Ephraim and Judah.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֥י כָעָ֖שׁ לְאֶפְרָ֑יִם וְכָרָקָ֖ב לְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, then Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot cure you or heal your wound.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim was a tribe in Israel.
Judah was another tribe in Israel.
Ephraim saw that he was sick.
Judah saw that he was wounded.
Ephraim went to Assyria for help.
Ephraim sent messengers to the great king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria could not cure Ephraim.
The king of Assyria could not heal Judah’s wound.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨רְא אֶפְרַ֜יִם אֶת־ חָלְי֗וֹ וִֽיהוּדָה֙ אֶת־ מְזֹר֔וֹ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יָרֵ֑ב וְה֗וּא לֹ֤א יוּכַל֙ לִרְפֹּ֣א לָכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ יִגְהֶ֥ה מִכֶּ֖ם מָזֽוֹר׃

passages.text: For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God compares Himself to a lion for Ephraim.
God compares Himself to a young lion for the house of Judah.
God says, "I will attack them and tear them apart."
God says, "I will leave after I attack."
God says, "I will carry them away."
No one will be able to rescue them from Me.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֤י כַשַּׁ֙חַל֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם וְכַכְּפִ֖יר לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲנִ֨י אֲנִ֤י אֶטְרֹף֙ וְאֵלֵ֔ךְ אֶשָּׂ֖א וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃

passages.text: Then I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, “I will go back to My place.
I will wait there.
I will stay away until the people admit their guilt.
They must confess their sins.
They must seek My face.
When they suffer trouble, they will look for Me.
In their distress, they will earnestly seek Me.”
passages.original: אֵלֵ֤ךְ אָשׁ֙וּבָה֙ אֶל־ מְקוֹמִ֔י עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר־ יֶאְשְׁמ֖וּ וּבִקְשׁ֣וּ פָנָ֑י בַּצַּ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם יְשַׁחֲרֻֽנְנִי׃
